# BioXtract

> BioXtract is a Radboud University spin-out developing a modular, nature-inspired
> biotechnology platform that uses targeted microbial bioleaching, sorption and
> selective dilution to recover and separate critical metals and rare earth elements
> (REEs) from electronic waste, printed circuit boards, mining effluents and other
> waste streams: a low-carbon alternative to conventional smelting and aggressive
> chemical leaching.

- **Website:** https://bioxtract.org
- **Contact:** contact@bioxtract.org
- **Based in:** Heyendaalseweg 135, 6525 AJ Nijmegen, The Netherlands
- **Parent institution:** Radboud University
- **Funder:** SPRIN-D, the German Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation, through the Tech Metal Transformation Challenge
- **License:** content on this site may be quoted with attribution to BioXtract

## What BioXtract does

BioXtract recovers critical metals and rare earth elements from e-waste, printed
circuit boards (PCBs), mining effluents and other suitable waste streams. Electronic waste contains
higher concentrations of gold, copper and REEs than most natural ores, yet most of it
is never recovered. Conventional recovery depends on energy-intensive smelting or
aggressive chemical leaching; BioXtract instead lets microbial redox chemistry do the
selective work under mild conditions with minimal chemical input.

Beyond recovery, the platform is designed for *directed metal transformation*: waste
can become a route to functional precursors for permanent magnets, luminescent
materials and other high-value applications.

## The platform: four stages, modular design

1. **Pre-treatment**. E-waste and PCBs need only minor pre-treatment, keeping energy
   costs and waste low.
2. **Microbial mobilization**. Microbial redox reactions act as catalysts to release
   critical elements from solid waste, avoiding the high energy and harsh chemicals
   consumption of traditional hydrometallurgy.
3. **Selective capture**. Targeted (bio)sorption recovers the leached metals,
   enriching specific elements by their affinity to organic or inorganic sorbents.
4. **Controlled separation**. Geochemical triggers (pH, ionic strength, competitive
   ligands and redox manipulation) drive sequential recovery. Organic and mineral
   sorbents are then regenerated and reused.

Each stage is self-contained and can slot into existing recycling lines, or the four
can chain into a continuous closed-loop system.

## Key facts

- 62 million tons of e-waste are generated globally each year, and less than 25% is
  formally collected and recycled. (Source: UN Global E-waste Monitor, 2024.)
- BioXtract's three defining properties are high selectivity, modular design, and
  resourceful, low-carbon operation under mild conditions.
- The team spans four continents and combines (geo)microbiology, biogeochemistry,
  mineralogy, reactive transport modeling, process engineering and knowledge transfer.

## The team

Managing Team: Dr Martyna Glodowska (CEO/CSO & Co-Founder), Pieter van der Velden
(CEO & Co-Founder), Dr Jessica Venetz (COO & Co-Founder). The R&D Team is co-led by
Dr Suzanne Haaijer-Vroomen and Dr Stian Torset.

BioXtract is advised by a Scientific Board (Dr James M. Byrne, University of Bristol;
Dr Bonnie McDevitt, USGS; Dr Anna Potysz, University of Wrocław; Dr Jeremiah Shuster,
University of Western Ontario; Dr Elizabeth J. Tomaszewski, USGS) and an Advisory
Board (Prof. Dr Henning Prommer, University of Western Australia / Ekion;
Prof. Dr Mario Zarroca Hernandez, Autonomous University of Barcelona).

The authoritative, always-current team list is published at
https://bioxtract.org/content/team.csv and rendered at https://bioxtract.org/#team
